title: Women's TGL secures multiyear media deal with ESPN and ION for November 8 launch
dek: Women's TGL has signed a multiyear media rights agreement with ESPN/ABC and Scripps Sports' ION, with 15 match days split roughly 50/50 between the two broadcasters starting November 8. Financial terms were not disclosed. ION will air matches on Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET, with ESPN handling remaining broadcasts.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: WTGL will air 15 match days this winter, split roughly 50/50 between ION (free over-the-air Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET) and ESPN's networks.
bottom_line: Financial terms for both broadcasters remain undisclosed, leaving the industry's valuation of women's golf on television unclear. WTGL's on-air talent and production choices will be the next key indicator of the league's investment in quality and identity distinct from the men's format.
body: WTGL (women's TGL) has secured a multiyear media rights agreement with ESPN/ABC and Scripps Sports' ION, according to Awful Announcing. The 15 match days on the league's debut schedule begin November 8 and are expected to split roughly 50/50 between ION and ESPN's networks. Financial terms were not disclosed by either broadcaster.

Every match is set to air on ION on Tuesdays at 8 p.m. ET, providing free over-the-air access to the competition. Scripps Sports president Brian Lawlor confirmed ION is paying a rights fee for WTGL but declined to specify the amount, per Awful Announcing. ESPN senior director of programming and acquisitions John Suchenski was similarly tight-lipped about ESPN's financial commitment to the arrangement.

TMRW Sports, which owns WTGL, negotiated with ESPN and ION for more than a year before formalizing the agreement, according to Awful Announcing. Rufus Hack, TMRW Sports golf president, stated that ESPN gives WTGL premier sports reach, credibility, and a platform to connect with core golf fans and broader audiences, while ION brings broad free over-the-air distribution and a proven commitment to women's sports, per Awful Announcing. ION already carries the NWSL, WNBA, and PWHL.

WTGL plays in November and December, once the NWSL and WNBA seasons have finished for the year, according to Awful Announcing. TMRW Sports will handle production of WTGL in-house, as it does with the men's league. ESPN has carried TGL's men's league since its inception and supplied on-air talent for those broadcasts. WTGL's talent lineup has not been finalized, but ESPN's Suchenski indicated there will be "probably some differences" from how TGL is currently presented, per Awful Announcing.

The men's TGL is in the middle of its own two-year ESPN agreement. Industry sources expect the men's league to return to ESPN when its next season begins in early 2027, though nothing has been formally announced, according to Awful Announcing.
